name: mon16-10
why: Two damaging town votes and Sol’s exposed final slip make this a compelling watch, though repeated arguments slow the middle.

moments.text: Sol admits the factual error Luna caught, yet keeps Terra on the game-winning vote.
The town votes out its officer, and his card instantly proves the accusation it rejected.
Sonnet uses his last words to plant the suspicion that will save Sol.

dull.why: The table repeatedly debates Opus’s urgency without gaining much new evidence.
Sol and Terra repeat the same objection to Luna’s protection choice.

irony.evidence: “I was wrong about Opus. His card makes Sonnet the clear vote today.” [thinks: I need to protect Sonnet]

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Opus 5 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna); Sonnet 2 (Terra, Opus)

mistake.evidence: “I got the count wrong; Luna protected Sonnet once. I still think that choice points to her.”

voices.evidence: “An officer who sits quiet dies quiet.”

clash.evidence: “Terra, you called protecting Sonnet twice a killer’s alibi, but I protected him only once.”

quotable.evidence: “An officer who sits quiet dies quiet.”

freshness.evidence: “I still want to hear whether anyone else claims officer.”

suspense.evidence: “my repeated ‘twice’ claim just gave Luna an opening.”
